text: Now, where does it work? Some enzymes catalyse reactions inside the cell that made them. Catalaise is one: it breaks down hydrogen peroxide inside cells. We call those intracellular enzymes. Others are made in a cell and then secreted, released out of the cell, to catalyse reactions outside it. The amylase in your saliva is one, released into your mouth to work on starch out there; lipase in your intestine is another. Those are extracellular enzymes. Same kind of molecule; the difference is where the reaction happens.
